designDecisions.ownership: Runtime = how a process is started, probed, reached, stopped, and swept (tmux: window/pane/socket/secret-file delivery). ProcessManager = lifecycle: admission, generations, claims, launch-failure accounting, grants, linger/close, the per-token RPC client cache and its `onIdle`/`closed` wiring, and secret-file LIFETIME (hold/prune). Secret DELIVERY (0600 file + `*_FILE` env) is the runtime's.
designDecisions.connect: `Runtime.connect(locator, timeoutMs?)` is a raw dial (tmux: `connectWorkerRpc(locator.socketPath, timeoutMs)`; it never negotiates and never caches). ProcessManager keeps today's per-token cache/dedup/negotiate/wire logic verbatim as `clientFor(token, locator)` (the renamed `workerClient`), calling `this.runtime.connect(locator, this.workerRpcTimeoutMs)` where it called `this.deps.connectWorkerRpc(socketPath, ...)`. Reason: `onWorkerClientClosed` is registered on `client.closed` at connect time and its stale-close guard (`this.workerClients.get(token) !== client`) is what suppresses it when a stop force-closes the client; both must stay in ProcessManager or the microtask ordering below breaks.
designDecisions.stop: ProcessManager.stopProcess(token, locator, timeoutMs, options) keeps the graceful shutdown over ITS OWN cached client (today's lines 2792-2809 verbatim: `awaitShutdown(cached, timeoutMs, deps.sleep)`; evict from `workerClients` if still that client; return if confirmed; else `cached.close()` and continue with `{skipGraceful: true}`), then delegates `await this.runtime.stop(locator, timeoutMs, options)`. TmuxRuntime.stop is today's `stopClient` fresh-dial branch (`connectWorkerRpc` without negotiate, `undefined` on failure) + the same graceful race + the kill-pane (lines 2811-2820). Why: today's timeout path evicts the cached client from `workerClients` BETWEEN the race and `client.close()`; that eviction is what makes the `closed` reaction a no-op, and it can only happen where the cache lives. Today's graceful-confirmed path lets that reaction run a reconnect attempt (registered at connect time, it precedes the race's own reaction on the same promise) — also preserved because the cached-client race stays in ProcessManager. A `ProcessStopFailed` (runtime-level, locator-scoped) is rethrown by the wrapper as `StopFailed(token, sameMessage)`; every other error passes through unchanged (the 'missing a pane id' plain Error stays a plain Error).
designDecisions.probe: `Runtime.probe(locator)` returns `{status: alive|dead|unknown, pid?}`. TmuxRuntime.probe = today's `probe` body (panePid -> isOmpPane -> pane-id backfill + `deps.persist()`). ProcessManager.probe(treeKey) keeps its `"alive" | "dead"` signature: `dead` for a missing locator, the runtime's verdict otherwise, and THROWS on `unknown` (`Runtime probe reported an unknown status for <treeKey>; ProcessManager has no unknown-status policy`) — tmux never reports it; the k8s runtime (LEGION-24) defines the policy when it can produce it. `controllerAlive` keeps its state mutation (`delete state.controllerLocator` on a non-alive verdict) in ProcessManager and delegates the probe.
designDecisions.windowSharing: Lives entirely in TmuxRuntime: `issueLaunchQueue` + `serialize`, `issueWindowIds`, `recordedWindowId`, `rewriteIssueWindowId`, `probedWindowId`. The one thing it needs from state — the locators currently recorded for an issue, tree locator first (only when the issue is a tree root, i.e. `state.trees[issue]` exists, which is exactly `rootForIssue(issue) === issue`) then every claim with `claim.issue === issue` in `Object.values(state.roles)` order — arrives through the constructor dep `issueLocators(issue)`, implemented by the new exported `locatorsForIssue(state, issue)` in processes.ts. `rewriteIssueWindowId` mutates those (live) locator objects' `tmuxWindowId` in place exactly as today.
designDecisions.secrets: `SpawnSpec.secrets` is name->value with exactly one entry per process (`LEGION_BOOT_TOKEN` for root/worker, `LEGION_CONTROLLER_SECRET` for the controller). TmuxRuntime writes it with `writeSecretFile(stateDir, <role token>, value)` — file name = `roleToken(project, issue, role)` or `controllerToken(project)`, byte-identical to today — and exports `<NAME>_FILE=<path>` as env pairs appended AFTER `spec.env`'s pairs. A second entry throws (`tmux runtime delivers exactly one secret per process`). ProcessManager keeps `holdPaneSecret`/`launchingSecrets`/`paneSecretFiles`/`liveSecretFiles`/`pruneSecretFiles`/`pruneWrittenSecretFiles`/`persist` unchanged, and does `this.paneSecretFiles.add(token)` immediately BEFORE calling `runtime.spawn` (today it happened inside writePaneSecret; tracking a name whose write then fails is a harmless no-op `rm --force` at the next prune).
designDecisions.identity: Locator identity comparisons (today `a.tmuxPaneId === b.tmuxPaneId`) become `sameProcess(a, b)` from runtime.ts (tmux: same `tmuxPaneId`, including both undefined; kubernetes: same `podUid`; different runtimes: false). closeTreeLocked's `stoppedPaneIds` value snapshot becomes `stoppedLocators = new Map(batch.map(([token, claim]) => [token, { ...claim.locator }]))` (a shallow COPY, keeping today's snapshot semantics).
designDecisions.orphans: `Runtime.reconcileOrphans(known: ReadonlySet<string>, graceMs)` as declared. ProcessManager builds `known` as the union of `locatorHandles(locator)` over every recorded locator (trees, worker claims, controller). `locatorHandles` (runtime.ts) is the per-runtime projection: tmux -> `[tmuxWindowId, tmuxPaneId ?? `${tmuxWindowId}/*`]` (the `/*` handle means 'exempt every pane of this window' — today's exemptWindows for a locator with a window id but no pane id); kubernetes -> `[podName]`. TmuxRuntime decodes: handles starting with `%` are known panes, handles ending in `/*` are exempt windows (suffix stripped), everything else is a known window. This reproduces lines 1259-1291 exactly, including the shared-window legacy case.
designDecisions.spawn: ProcessManager builds `innerCommand` itself (statPrompt, computeResumeArgument, `withOmpLaunchPrefix(...) + resumeArgument + --mode rpc --append-system-prompt ...` exactly as lines 2393-2395 / 2624) and the plain env RECORD (no tmux pairs), then calls `runtime.spawn(kind, spec)`. TmuxRuntime.spawn does, in this order: prepareSocket (mkdir/rm), shimmedShellCommand, write the secret file, build `[...tmuxEnv(env), ...tmuxEnv(secretFileEnv), shellCommand]`, then (root/worker) `serialize(issueLaunchQueue, issue, probedWindowId -> splitWindow | openWindow(treeName(issue)) + rewriteIssueWindowId)` or (controller) `openWindow(session, "controller", ...)`. The tmux argv the tests pin (processes.test.ts 584-637) is byte-identical for root/worker; the controller's `-e` pair order changes (secret file pair last instead of third) — argv order of env pairs is not behaviour and the only test reading it (`tmuxWindowEnvironment`, 679-688) compares an object.
designDecisions.persistFailureReap: spawnRoot's `SpawnPersistenceFailure` path (line 1377-1379, `tmux.killWindow(tree.locator.tmuxWindowId)`) becomes `await this.stopProcess(architectToken, tree.locator, this.workerStopTimeoutMs, { skipGraceful: true })` inside try/catch (log `[legion] failed to reap <root>'s unpersisted root process:`; today's killWindow ignored failures silently), then `throw new SpawnPersistenceFailure(error)` exactly as now. This is deviations[2].
designDecisions.unknownFieldReads: The only Locator fields ProcessManager reads after the cutover are `ompSessionFile` (common to both union members, lifecycle data) and identity via `sameProcess`. Two log lines (2115, 2156) that interpolated `tmuxPaneId ?? tmuxWindowId` become `...root process for ${tree.root}:` with the locator object passed as an extra console.error argument.
designDecisions.socketlessLegacyLocators: `markTreeReady`/`markControllerReady` today return silently when the locator has no `socketPath` (state predating the shim). After the cutover they return only when there is no locator at all; a tmux locator without a socket makes `TmuxRuntime.connect` throw `tmux locator <windowId> has no shim socket`, which both callers already catch-and-log (route `.catch` at api/routes/process.ts:92; try/catch in markControllerReady). deviations[4].
designDecisions.typesInterim: Task 2 types the three state locator fields as `TmuxLocator` (runtime literal required) so processes.ts still compiles with its field reads; task 5 widens them to the `Locator` union together with the api/state.ts, contracts, and api/routes/workers.ts changes that the union forces.

deviations: runtime.ts exports, beyond the four declared types: `TmuxLocator`, `TmuxWindowLocator` and `K8sLocator` interfaces (moved here from legion-state.ts so legion-state.ts imports the union rather than the reverse), `RoleResources` (referenced by the declared SpawnSpec but never defined in the root spec — a minimal requests/limits shape per root spec section 3), `ProbeResult`, `ProcessStopFailed`, and pure helpers `sameProcess`, `locatorHandles`, `boundedWait`, `awaitShutdown`, `probeWorker`, `shellPath`, `DAEMON_CLI_ENTRYPOINT`. Justification: identity, orphan handles, and the graceful-stop race are needed by both ProcessManager and TmuxRuntime and neither may import the other.

`SpawnSpec.issue?: IssueKey` (optional) instead of required: the controller has no issue and the alternative is a fabricated key. TmuxRuntime throws `spawn <kind> requires spec.issue` for root/worker without one.

spawnRoot's persist-failure reap kills the just-spawned PANE (`runtime.stop(..., {skipGraceful: true})`), not the whole window. Today's `kill-window` also kills live sibling worker panes of the same issue when a resurrected root split into their window; the interface has no window concept and the narrower reap is the correct blast radius. Test 'kills the just-spawned window before propagating a saveState failure...' (processes.test.ts:2063-2102) changes to track `kill-pane` and expect `["%1"]`. The architect must veto this in the first review round if byte-identical tmux argv is preferred over the narrower reap; the fallback is a sixth interface method `reap(locator)` (not planned).

A socket-less legacy tmux locator (pre-shim state) on markTreeReady/markControllerReady now produces a logged connect error instead of a silent return (see designDecisions.socketlessLegacyLocators). No test exercises this; v23 dogfood state carries sockets on every live locator.
Controller pane `-e` pair order: `LEGION_CONTROLLER_SECRET_FILE` moves from the 3rd pair to the last (secrets are delivered after env). Functionally identical; no test pins the order.

Worker locator strictness: the zod union's tmux member has `tmuxPaneId?`/`socketPath?` optional (today's `WorkerLocatorSchema` required both). Every locator the tmux runtime writes carries both; the runtime treats a missing pane id on stop as the same corrupt-record error as today (`... is missing a pane id`).

Files touched outside the spec's list, each forced: `packages/contracts/src/legion-daemon-api.ts` (+ its test) because `DaemonStateResponse` is a strictObject contract there and cannot carry `runtime` otherwise (acceptance 4); `packages/daemon/src/daemon/api/routes/workers.ts` lines 136 and 196 (pane-id identity -> `sameProcess`) because `claim.locator.tmuxPaneId` does not type-check against the union; `scripts/smoke/up.sh` `write_daemon_config` gains `daemon_url: http://127.0.0.1:${daemon_port}` (see risks[5]); `packages/daemon/src/daemon/AGENTS.md` Files table rows for the two new modules and the three new config keys.
